# Tread

> Tread is a small, statically typed programming language built to teach how programming languages work. Its toolchain is written in Go: a lexer, parser, type checker, bytecode compiler, and stack-based virtual machine, each a separate package small enough to read.

Key facts (updated 2026-11-13):

- Motto: "A language for learning how languages work." A tread is one step of a staircase; Tread is learned one stage at a time: lexer, parser, checker, compiler, VM.
- Command: `tread`, with `tread run <file.tr|file.tbc>`, `tread check <file.tr>`, `tread build <file.tr>` (compiles to a `.tbc` bytecode file), `tread new <name>`, `tread doctor`, `tread version`, and `tread help`. Source files use the `.tr` extension.
- Error codes: `TR-` plus a phase letter and a number, for example `TR-T001` (type mismatch) or `TR-R003` (call depth exceeded). Runtime errors inside a function print a stack trace.
- Version 0.6.0, released 2026-11-13, experimental. Two editions need no Go: the Tread SDK (compiler and runtime) and the Tread Runtime (runs `.tbc` files only), as archives and installers (.msi, .pkg, .deb, .rpm, install.sh, install.ps1): https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/releases/tag/v0.6.0 . With Go 1.25 or later: `go install github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/cmd/tread@v0.6.0`.
- Language today: types Int, Float, Bool, String, Unit; `let` and `let mut`; functions with typed parameters and recursion; if / else if / else; `while` and `for` loops with `break` and `continue`; `Array<T>` and `Map<K, V>` with value semantics; enums with payloads and an exhaustive `match`; generic functions, enums and structs; the built-in `Option<T>`; structs with methods in `impl` blocks (`self`, `mut self`); multi-file programs with `import a.b` and `pub`; string interpolation with `${...}`; `print` and `toString`; checked integer arithmetic.
- Not supported yet: function values, `Result` error handling, a package manager, and file or network I/O.
- Platforms: macOS 12 or later (Apple silicon, Intel), Linux kernel 3.2 or later (x86-64, ARM64), Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later (x86-64).
- Free and open source under the MIT License. Created by Sarvess Veeriyah.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md): overview, installation, quick start, and full guide
- [README as Markdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/main/README.md): the same guide as plain Markdown
- [Installation](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md#installation): installers and install scripts, SDK and Runtime archives, go install, building from source
- [Language tutorial](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md#language-tutorial): seventeen short lessons, each a complete program with its output
- [Language reference](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md#language-reference): types, operators, keywords, scope
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md#cli-reference): commands, behaviour, exit codes
- [Errors and diagnostics](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/README.md#errors-and-diagnostics): error format, code families, stack traces

## Optional

- [Playground](https://treadlang.vercel.app/compile/): run Tread in the browser with the real compiler and VM (WebAssembly); shows tokens, AST and bytecode
- [Download](https://treadlang.vercel.app/download/): Tread SDK and Tread Runtime installers (.msi, .pkg, .deb, .rpm), archives, and install scripts
- [Changelog](https://treadlang.vercel.app/changelog/): every user-visible change, by release ([source](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md))
- [Source code](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/tree/main): compiler, virtual machine, CLI, and tests
- [Issues](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/Tread/issues): bug reports and feature requests
- [Website](https://treadlang.vercel.app/): overview, examples, architecture, and FAQ
